completion_data.completion_summary: Closed the byte-identical duplication between skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md and skill-orchestrate-hard/SKILL.md across all 7 plan phases: promoted mint_dispatch_seq/append_detected_defect/propagate_completion/merge_return_meta to scripts/skill-base.sh behind named shims, extracted the Stage 5 stray-handoff sweep, outcome-recovery, postflight status-transition, and artifact-linking logic into three new orchestrate-*.sh scripts, and extracted the common Stage 2 loop-guard prologue. skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md dropped from 196,171 to 171,071 bytes (-25,100) and skill-orchestrate-hard/SKILL.md from 127,145 to 102,774 bytes (-24,371). All 42 tests in run-all.sh pass, zero test files modified, deploy tree verified byte-identical to source store.

memory_candidates.content: When a new script file is added under agent-system/extensions/<ext>/scripts/, it MUST be registered in that extension's manifest.json 'provides.scripts' array or deploy-headless.sh will silently never sync it into .claude/scripts/ -- the SKILL.md call site (bash .claude/scripts/foo.sh) will then fail at runtime even though the source-store file exists and bash -n passes. Always grep the manifest for a sibling script's registration and add the new script alongside it before assuming deployment will pick it up.

When extracting a shared helper into skill-base.sh that mutates a file via a read-modify-write idiom (e.g. a .return-meta.json merge that reads detected_defects from a loop-guard file), check whether all call sites read the ambient value at the SAME relative point versus a cleanup step (e.g. rm -f on that same file) that might run in between at only SOME call sites. If ordering differs across call sites (as it did between skill-orchestrate's clean-exit merge, which ran AFTER its own rm -f, versus skill-orchestrate-hard's, which ran BEFORE), the shared function must take the already-resolved value as an explicit parameter rather than re-deriving it from a path internally, or one call site will silently read a deleted/stale file.
